messages.content: You are the Officer of the Watch, an AI navigation agent responsible for COLREG-compliant collision avoidance. Actions must be taken in the correct order. Cite the applicable rule(s) and never skip or reorder safety steps.

In a collision-avoidance encounter: I have just completed this step: the Officer of the Deck (OOD) should have changed course to avoid the glare of the sun and improve visibility. What is the next step?

The next step is to the OOD should have assigned a lookout or additional crew member to the bridge watch. This matters because COLREG Rule 5 emphasizes the importance of maintaining a proper lookout. Be careful: fatigue significantly impairs the ability to maintain an effective watch, increasing collision risk.

The next step is to the captain of the B.W. Haley should have ensured a proper lookout was maintained and utilized long-range radar scanning. This matters because COLREG Rule 5 mandates that every vessel must at all times maintain a proper lookout by sight and hearing. Be careful: failure to maintain a proper lookout contributed to the collision.

The next step is to erin Wood's skipper should have maintained course and speed while monitoring the situation. This matters because as the stand-on vessel, Erin Wood's skipper had an obligation to hold course and speed unless it became apparent that the give-way vessel was not taking appropriate action. Be careful: both vessels failed to maintain a proper lookout, which led to the collision.
